node: Export controls, sanctions, and procurement compliance software/services
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around compliance workload created by tariffs, sanctions, export controls, denied-party screening, and defense-industrial supply-chain visibility. The strongest public-market mapping is not defense primes but niche trade-compliance data/software and advisory providers. Reference leaders include Thomson Reuters and RELX/LexisNexis because they own broad sanctions and restricted-party data platforms. The more underfollowed lane is Descartes Systems Group and FTI Consulting: Descartes has unusually direct exposure through denied-party screening and global trade compliance software, while FTI has services exposure to export-control and sanctions compliance programs. Evidence remains mixed: the macro burden is supported by recent defense-industry commentary, but company-level revenue sensitivity to this node needs segment disclosure, customer mix, and growth-rate verification.
